If creation/inspection leaves insufficient full preparation window, cleanup without preparation.
bootstrap.delivery: Future authorized workspace creator supplies fixed owner source as immutable container-create Cmd; validates exact inspected entrypoint/Cmd/image/env/policy before sole start. Same immutable pinned image; never rebuild, copy, mount, exec-upload, stdin-source or tmpfs script.
bootstrap.delivery_boundary: NEW additive fixed bootstrap adapter is an explicit effect/input boundary. Its future separately authorized workspace-creation/launch admission must bind actual source bytes/hash/size and exact Cmd before create/start. Neither historical provider authority nor preparation facets authorize this bootstrap. This selection issues no bootstrap authority; missing fixed launch authorization/identity fails PROOF_UNRESOLVED before creation. No additional generalized source-delivery authority selected.
bootstrap.inspection: New additive pure inspector compares every frozen sandbox dimension and actual source Cmd plus Tty/OpenStdin/StdinOnce/RestartPolicy/RestartCount. Existing exact-source safe_configuration must remain unchanged; no claim it already accepts new controller.
bootstrap.native_argv_limit: Before create, compute exact platform-native serialized argv, including Docker prefix/options and quoted source. Require Windows CreateProcess command line <32767 UTF-16 code units including terminator and Linux single-argument/system limits. bootstrap.source_argument: Exact future reviewed fixed source bytes, decoded strict UTF-8 and roundtrip-equal, as ONE argv element; no NUL/BOM, formatting, interpolation or caller input. No extra argv.
bootstrap.source_location_container: No filesystem source path: exact Docker Config.Cmd[-1] input to Python -c, code filename <string>, resident interpreter memory. Never claim embedded in image.
bootstrap.start_channel: Exactly one fixed start --attach --interactive against owner-retained inspected full 64-lowercase-hex container ID; split stdout/stderr, no PTY, no generic attach/exec method exposed. No reattach/start retry after ambiguity.

criteria.challenge_sequence: Same serial state retains strict sequence, used IDs and owner-issued 32-byte challenges; no disk/session restore.
criteria.child_supervision: PID1 launches only frozen javac argv in a new session/process group under existing pids/memory/cpu/seccomp constraints.
criteria.cleanup_after_loss: Independent retained cleanup identity is required after inner failure, but concrete backend-generation authentication for full-ID kill/remove is missing. Candidate not finally selected.
criteria.closed_environment: Exact eight-variable environment, no identifiers or deadlines added as environment variables.
criteria.complexity: Smallest supported evolution: one inner event loop plus fixed host adapter and independent outer custodian.
criteria.controller_generation: One live PID1 process and unbroken owner-held channel, source/executable/image and kernel incarnation bound together; PID alone insufficient.
criteria.disconnect: Any EOF, malformed frame, capture failure or attach loss invalidates owner relation; independent outer teardown follows.
criteria.local_fence: Single selector state machine; coherent snapshot or one active mutation/reservation; priority cleanup installs permanent barrier.
criteria.no_network: Inherited stdio pipes only; no socket/socketpair/network syscall required.
criteria.observation_coherence: Snapshot runs only while compiler is fully reaped and no mutation/reservation race exists; incomplete writer/mount/task inventory fails unresolved.
criteria.readonly_root_exact_tmpfs: Inline fixed Python -c source creates no infrastructure files; exact immutable root and tmpfs options unchanged.
criteria.reconnect_resurrection: No reconnect, reattach, restart or restored generation; replacements require new workspace issuance after old cleanup.
criteria.sandbox2_change: None. Existing policy permits pipes/selectors/setsid/kill/wait and ordinary child creation; future live validation remains mandatory.
criteria.single_active_mutation: One active operation ID or one exclusive handoff identity, never both; ordinary extra requests fail closed.
criteria.workspace_continuity: Same /work and /tmp mounts, container and controller from empty observation through preparation and reservation; no artifact export.

challenge.issuer: original workspace owner using unpredictable OS entropy
challenge.observation_only: Non-null request challenge exactly for frozen three OBSERVE tags. Mutation poststate uses separate spent-admission post-observation reference exactly as frozen schema; no new wire challenge field. Validate entire response once, consume before readiness; stale or duplicate response cannot restore state.
challenge.sequence: Strictly increasing positive_int, exactly previous accepted+1; bounded by frozen integer maximum, exhaustion terminal. Single-use IDs/challenges; no reset/retry/replay after loss.

child_process.attempt_deadline_origin: One host-monotonic preparation admission instant before materialization; compiler shares remaining budget, never resets. First inner materialization fixes <=5000ms inner budget; host independently enforces original absolute deadline including transport latency.
child_process.cleanup_budget: All cancellation/reaping/EOF closure must fit remaining original <=10000ms hard preparation deadline and retained cleanup reserve. Existing 1s wait/.25s reap are maximum sub-budgets clamped to original hard deadline, never appended past it.
child_process.constraint_support: Current SANDBOX.2 default allow with namespace-clone denials and clone3 ENOSYS retains ordinary child creation/setsid/pipe/select/read/wait/kill; pids=128/memory=128MiB/cpu=1 unchanged. JAVA.1C selector capture supplies source-level precedent, not a new live proof. New implementation must fail rather than widen if actual limits are insufficient.
child_process.ownership: Persistent single-thread PID1 owns javac session/process group; stays PID1 to adopt orphaned group descendants. Nonblocking bounded pipe selectors share attempt deadline and prioritize cleanup input. Kill group even after parent exit; wait direct child, waitpid group adopted descendants, prove no group/task/writer remains, observe both EOFs, close pipes/selectors. No target JVM launch.
child_process.success: Exact source/materialization remains same controller/workspace generation; compiler exit=0, empty complete captures, both EOFs, no lingering group, unchanged 239-byte source and exact one bounded class. Inert metadata parsing only. Controller stays alive until handoff/cleanup/retention limit.

selection.cleanup_response_composition: Logical controller boundary includes host adapter: inner CLEANUP_AND_REPORT produces exactly one bounded frozen response with partial evidence and PROOF_UNRESOLVED until outer outcomes exist. Host adapter retains it, invokes custodian independently, and returns one separately provenance-bound composite typed result to owning workspace (in-process, not a second inner wire response). Inner never claims COMPLETE after its own removal. Components use frozen cleanup_evidence/outer schemas and exact original IDs; missing child/EOF facts remain unresolved even with outer absence. No new semantic field or readiness is inferred.

disconnect_reconnect.response: Host fence permanently invalidates capability/generations before attempting cancellation; inner installs barrier if EOF/cancellation observed. Docker attach disconnect is NOT guaranteed to deliver immediate inner EOF: independent outer custodian kills/removes exact container, and inner startup watchdog bounds disconnected survival. Readiness cannot depend on reconnect.

local_fence.admission: Original workspace/preparation owners independently authenticate/spend their own facets. Fixed host adapter checks original single-use admission relation before forwarding; no caller receives raw stdin/argv. Scalar admission ID alone grants nothing. Inner pins relation and checks exact operation, generation, IDs/sequence, manifest and local state before effect.
local_fence.cleanup: Validated priority BEGIN_CLEANUP, EOF, local deadline or outer cancellation installs/increments permanent cleanup barrier first, withdraws readiness, cancels operation/handoff, kills group and reaps/closes captures, then reports. Never BUSY while leaving readiness. After barrier only cleanup/evidence paths; no new observation-for-readiness, materialization, compile or handoff.
local_fence.cooperation: Materialization uses bounded descriptor operations and checks control/deadline between steps; compile integrates stdin, child pipes and child status in selector. Existing blocking capture_process is evidence/pattern, not reused unchanged for preemption.
local_fence.mutual_exclusion: At most one mutation or exclusive handoff; observation runs only quiescent after full child reaping and under same fence. No observation queued behind active mutation. Active ID and handoff identity are complete snapshot fields.
local_fence.no_cross_owner_atomicity: No private cross-owner locks or transactional claims. Immediately reauthenticate original operation-bound admission and current upstream eligibility at effect/handoff boundary; any unobservable gap fails PROOF_UNRESOLVED before effect. Late loss stops subsequent effects; no facet refund/retry.
local_fence.placement: One PID1 selector event loop plus host adapter admission state for its exact single channel; no threads/background workers or locks shared with other owners.

outer_cleanup.absence: Only independently authenticated exact-ID not-found on same provable backend relation establishes absence; timeout, connection error, wrong backend, empty response or generic nonzero does not. Removal and fresh absence are distinct. Neither proves lost child wait/EOF; composite preserves unresolved components.
outer_cleanup.bootstrap_failure: Custodian must retain returned full ID before start; if create response lost and full identity cannot be safely recovered via authorized creation relation, report cleanup unresolved, never guess a name/target.
outer_cleanup.fixed_control: Exact full-ID inspect, kill and rm --force --volumes only behind TERMINATE; separate exact full-ID absence inspection behind OBSERVE. No generic Docker API/passthrough. Cleanup retries bounded by fixed original identity and cleanup budget; any backend-generation ambiguity yields unresolved targeting.
outer_cleanup.independence: Custodian has its own fixed bounded backend operations/control handle and retained identity; no inner channel, live workspace readiness, upstream ISSUED status or unspent facet required. Host-loop cleanup works after inner/attach loss. Entire host loss does not magically preserve in-memory authority: independent startup watchdog stops inner, external supervision or later safe cleanup proof remains unresolved; no persisted JSON authority restore.
outer_cleanup.target_supply: Creator receives full 64-lowercase-hex container ID; independent inspect must match exact ID, immutable image/config and authorized creation relation before start. Before starting, custodian retains immutable original backend/generation/full-ID cleanup relation in its own host registry. Public input is only frozen authenticated retained relation plus fresh request ID/barrier; never caller target, name, Docker prefix or command.

retained_lifetime.admission: Do not start preparation unless full remaining <=10s hard window fits before work cutoff; request and observation budgets may shorten but never extend total. Reservation/consumer work must fit before work cutoff; no consumer authority is supplied here.
retained_lifetime.enforcement: Workspace-owning foreground event loop selects on channel/deadlines; no detached worker or returning live capability after scope ends. At work cutoff or earlier completion/failure/abandonment/upstream loss set barrier, withdraw readiness, cancel handoff/operation and run cleanup. Inner has independent <=30s startup watchdog for disconnected execution. Its origin is actual inner startup, so after total host loss it may fire later than host creation-origin deadline; it NEVER grants readiness beyond host cutoff and does not prove physical absence by host deadline. No host/inner clock equality or hidden deadline transfer claim.
retained_lifetime.expiration: By total deadline no intentional readiness, handoff or running work is permitted. If backend removal/absence cannot be proved within reserve, retain terminal cleanup obligation and report WORKSPACE_CLEANUP_UNRESOLVED; never claim physical absence or extend/renew capability. Any later exact-identity cleanup retry is cleanup-only, not retained readiness.
retained_lifetime.liveness: Timestamps and deadline values bound policy only; fresh challenge plus original live relation still required.
retained_lifetime.rationale: Small practical foreground envelope: up to existing 10s hard preparation window plus up to 10s bounded creation/observation/reservation slack, followed by 10s cleanup reserve. No idle service or indefinite ready retention.
retained_lifetime.start: Host monotonic instant immediately BEFORE first container creation attempt, bound to original workspace/controller relation. Creation/start/empty observation consume the same total lifetime.

transport_candidates.reason: Existing exact inline controller/start-attach pattern; pipes need no new syscalls, mounts or files. Safe independent outer cleanup and aggregate budget feasibility are not yet resolved.

wire.admission_boundary: Before dispatch reject any already-buffered/readable unexpected trailing input. An unbounded future stream cannot be proved empty forever: later invalid bytes install terminal barrier/cancel and suppress success, never claim to undo an already admitted effect. A second ordinary frame cannot grant another effect.
wire.canonical_encoding: UTF-8 JSON; sort_keys=true; separators=(',', ':'); ensure_ascii=true; allow_nan=false; exact schema types and list order; no Unicode normalization
wire.cardinality: Exactly one terminal semantic response for each admitted complete request if channel survives; no unsolicited messages. Loss may prevent response; never retry an uncertain effect. Multiple sequential request/response pairs in one lifetime/channel.
wire.duplicate_trailing: Track request_id and operation_id across entire nonrenewable generation; reused IDs/sequences are rejected without repeating effects. Bytes beyond an announced body are either a permitted next complete frame at its admission point, the sole priority cleanup frame, or fatal unexpected/trailing data; never ignored.
wire.eof: Any EOF, including frame-boundary EOF, is terminal: barrier, invalidate, cancel, cleanup. Partial header/body is protocol failure. Successful final cleanup report followed by EOF is normal terminal closure, never retained readiness.
wire.frame_bound_reason: Frozen schema says all frames <=8192, so header is included; never silently allow 8196.
wire.length_encoding: unsigned 32-bit big-endian binary, exactly four octets
wire.ordering: Complete frames never interleave and responses remain FIFO. No logical multiplex, response reordering, general queue or concurrent mutation streams.
wire.partial_timeout_rule: Header/body assembly starts at first byte, uses one 1000ms absolute deadline (not reset per byte), further limited by operation/preparation/retention deadline; a stalled cleanup frame triggers outer cleanup.
wire.priority_basis: Frozen contract minimum_operation_review.cleanup_split requires preemption without waiting for active effect completion. FIFO control pipelining has no independently multiplexed stream and adds no semantic fields or operations.
wire.priority_control_exception: Only one complete BEGIN_CLEANUP may follow one pending ordinary request. It belongs to the same serial state machine; validate and set barrier before waiting for active work. If original reply has not started, finish original with frozen typed failure, then cleanup response in FIFO order. No second mutation or observation is admitted. Any other extra/duplicate frame is fatal. If original reply bytes already started, finish that bounded frame without rewriting bytes; host barrier suppresses its readiness/success publication and no receipt is issued, then deliver cleanup reply. No cross-owner rollback is claimed.
wire.reader: Accumulate exactly four header bytes then exactly declared payload; bounded storage, no overread-as-new-request. Partial reads wait only to current absolute deadline. Zero/oversize rejected before allocation or effect. No raw command interpretation.
wire.semantic_validation: Reject BOM, malformed UTF-8, duplicate keys at all depths, unknown/missing keys, bool-as-int, coercion, NaN/infinity, trailing JSON/whitespace and noncanonical byte serialization. Compare validated re-encoding to original payload before operation admission.
wire.stream_budgets: No logging on controller stdout; controller stderr empty on success. Child streams separate. Keep <=8192 captured bytes per outer stream cumulatively over whole preparation attempt, INCLUDING wire headers; no reset at materialize/compile/observation boundaries. Also cap entire retained session at 65536 outer bytes per direction and 64 requests, including cleanup. Reserve two request slots for BEGIN_CLEANUP and CLEANUP_AND_REPORT plus bounded cleanup/error response budget before ordinary admission. If complete evidence or cumulative budget cannot fit, fail closed and use independent outer teardown; no truncation or success. Separate session budget never relaxes preparation budget.
wire.version_reason: Authenticated fixed launch/channel selects this framing ID; canonical semantic envelope already carries exact protocol_id and version=1. Redundant magic/version adds no boundary.
